characterization_methods.key_findings: Dark blocky/elongated δ-ferrite dendrites embedded in a lighter γ austenite matrix; significant dendrite fractions; 27% δ-ferrite retained at room temperature.
characterization_methods.purpose: reveal the as-cast solidified microstructure (δ-ferrite dendrites in γ austenite matrix)

computational_details.boundary_and_initial_conditions: Pseudo-binary phase diagram for the multicomponent system at the alloy composition (0.8 wt% C), temperature range 600–1400 °C.
computational_details.simulation_method: Thermodynamic calculation (pseudo-binary phase diagram and phase-fraction evolution)
computational_details.validation_against_experiment: Outputs are consistent with Ref. [15] for the same alloy composition.

interfaces.phase_evolution: δ-ferrite nucleates directly from the liquid phase at high temperature; during the next stage, liquid and δ-ferrite combine to form γ by peritectic reaction; thickening of γ-solid at liquid/δ-ferrite phase interfaces blocks solute exchange, causing cessation of δ-ferrite decomposition by incomplete peritectic reaction, leaving 27% δ-ferrite in equilibrium with γ at room temperature.

processing_steps.atmosphere: 10^-5 mbar pressure, backfilled with argon gas atmosphere
processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: Remelted 5–6 times inside the arc melter (AM500-Edmund Buhler GmbH, Germany) without breaking the vacuum for better elemental intermixing.

structures.overall_structure: As-cast solidified microstructure consisting of δ-ferrite dendrites embedded in an austenite (γ) matrix; dendrite fractions are significant and 27% δ-ferrite remains at room temperature in equilibrium with the γ phase.

unmapped_findings: Rough estimation with software reveals that dendrite fractions reduce from 27% in the as-cast microstructure to 19% after hot rolling (b0018).

The as-cast sample contains δ-ferrite rather than B2; B2 forms subsequently when δ-ferrite transforms to B2 through the order-disordered transition at 1125 °C during homogenization at 1150 °C for 2 h (b0017).
